questions.question: In a 1200 m circular race, A and B start at the same time from the same position in the same direction at speeds of 18 km/h and 27 km/h, respectively. In how much time after the start of race will they meet for the first time on the track?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

A and B running in the same direction, their relative speed = (27 - 18) = 9 km/hr = 9 km/hr × 5/18 = 2.5 m/s

They start at the same time, so they meet after 1200/2.5 = 480 seconds

∴ The correct answer is 480 seconds

questions.question: A bus driver must complete a 240 km trip in 4 hours. If he averages 70 km an hour for the first 3 hours of his trip. how fast must he travel (in km/h) in the last/final hour?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A bus driver must complete a 240 km trip in 4 hours. He averages 70 km/h for the first 3 hours of his trip.

**Concept:**

To find the required speed for the last hour, we need to determine the remaining distance and then calculate the speed needed to cover that distance in the remaining time.

**Calculation:**

Total distance to be covered = 240 km

Total time available = 4 hours

Distance covered in the first 3 hours:

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 70 km/h × 3 hours

⇒ Distance = 210 km

Remaining distance to be covered in the final hour:

⇒ Remaining distance = Total distance - Distance covered in the first 3 hours

⇒ Remaining distance = 240 km - 210 km

⇒ Remaining distance = 30 km

Speed required to cover the remaining distance in the final hour:

⇒ Speed = Distance / Time

⇒ Speed = 30 km / 1 hour

⇒ Speed = 30 km/h

**∴ The bus driver must travel at 30 km/h in the last hour.**

questions.question: Ruksana travelled at 60 km/h while going from point A to point B and returned via the same route at a different speed. If Ruksana’s overall average speed during the two-way journey was 48 km/h, what was her speed while travelling from B to A?
questions.solution:
Given:

The speed of the car is travelling is 60 km/hr and Average Speed is 48 km/hr

Formula used:

Average speed = Total distance/Total time

Time = Distance/Speed

Calculation:

Let the Speed for returning be S.

Let the distance between A and B be x

2x/48 = x/60 + x/S

⇒ 2x/48 - x/60 = x/S

⇒ x/24 - x/60 = x/S

⇒3x/120 = x/S

⇒S = 40 km/h

Required speed = S = 40 km/hr

∴ The Required speed for returning is 40 km/hr.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Calculation:

⇒ (2 × S₁ × S₂)/(S₁ + S₂) = Average speed

⇒ (2 × 60 × S2)/(60 + S2) = 48

⇒ 5 × S₂ = 120 + 2 × S₂

⇒ 3 × S2 = 120

⇒ S2 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/h.**

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 40 km in 24 minutes. If its speed is decreased by 40 km/hr, then what will be the time taken by it to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Speed = 40 ÷ (24/60) = 100 km/hr.

New Speed = 100 − 40 = 60 km/hr.

New Time = 40 ÷ 60 hours = (40 ÷ 60) × 60 minutes.

New Time = 40 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70bc0e4e249c09d59a1b6311e802d7411a41b85aa8b7e492be09784d4849e447.png] 

**Given:**

Distance = 40 km

Initial time = 24 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Initial time in hours = 24 ÷ 60 = 2/5 hours

⇒ Initial speed = 40 ÷ (2/5) = 100 km/hr

⇒ Decreased speed = 100 − 40 = 60 km/hr

⇒ New time taken = Distance ÷ New speed

⇒ New time = 40 ÷ 60 hours

⇒ New time in minutes = (40 ÷ 60) × 60 = 40 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 40 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If the distance covered is equal in both parts of the journey, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

questions.question: Malay walks around a circular field at the rate of 7 rounds per hour, while Neha runs around it at the rate of 11 rounds per hour. They start in the same direction from the same point at 02:45 p.m. They shall first cross each other at:

Malay speed round a circular field = 7 rounds per hour.

Neha speed round a circular field = 11 rounds per hour

they start at 2:45 p.m. in the same direction. 

**FORMULA USED:**

Relative speeds when moving in the same direction = difference of speeds.

**CALCULATION :**

The relative speed between Malay and Neha = 11 - 7 = 4 rounds/h (as they are in the same direction )

Time taken to complete one round at this speed = 1/4 hr

⇒ (1/4) × 60 min

⇒ 15 min.

So, 2:45 + 15 min = 3:00 p.m.

**∴ They shall first cross each other after 15 minutes i.e. at 03:00 p.m.**

questions.question: Ali and Badal start from the same position and at the same time in a 1200 m circular race, with speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. Find after how much time they will meet again on the track for the first time when they are both running in the same direction.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ali and Badal start from the same position and at the same time in a 1200 m circular race, with speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. 

**Calculations:**

Relative speed of both in same direction = S2-S1=45 - 27 =18 km/h = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s.

So,

Time taken by them to meet for the first time on the track while running in same direction = Length of track / relative speed in same direction = 1200/5= 240 seconds 

**Hence, The Required time is 240 seconds.**

questions.question: A train covers the distance between two stations X and Y in 6 hours. If the speed of the train is reduced by 13 km/h, then it travels the same distance in 9 hours. Find the distance between the two stations
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A train covers the distance between two stations X and Y in 6 hours. If the speed of the train is reduced by 13 km/h, then it travels the same distance in 9 hours.

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time taken

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between the station X and Y be d and the initial speed of the train be v

Then, d = 6v

When the speed of the train is reduced by 13km/h, the equation can be written as d = 9(v-13).

Substituting v=(d)/(6) in the above equation and solving for d,

d=9( (d)/(6) -13)

d=(3d)/(2) -117

d = 234km

**∴ The distance between the two stations is 234 km.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Let the initial speed be x

Distance = Speed × Time 

According to the question,

⇒ x × 6 = (x - 13) × 9

⇒ 6x = 9x - 117

⇒ 3x = 117

⇒ x = 39 kmph

Distance = 39 × 6 = 234 km. 

∴ The distance between the two stations is 234 km.

questions.question: A police travelling at 65 km/h is chasing a thief who is 1200 m away from him and is travelling at 41 km/h. Find the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the policeman = 65 km/h

Speed of the thief = 41 km/h

Distance between the policeman and the thief = 1200 m

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = Speed of the policeman - Speed of the thief

Relative speed = 65 - 41

Relative speed = 24 km/h

Convert 1200 m to km:

1200 m = 1200 / 1000 km = 1.2 km

Time taken to catch the thief = Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 1.2 km / 24 km/h

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 1.2 / 24

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = 0.05 hours

Convert
 hours to minutes:

0.05 hours × 60 minutes/hour = 3 minutes

**The time taken by the policeman to catch the thief is 3 minutes.**

questions.question: A policeman is chasing a thief at a speed of 12 km/h, and the thief is running at a speed of 8 km/h. If the policeman started 30 minutes late, find the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed = Policeman speed − Thief speed = 12 − 8 = 4 km/h.

Time in minutes = 1 × 60 = 60 minutes.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ − V₂.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other or away from each other in opposite directions, the relative speed is the sum: Vᵣₑₗ = V₁ + V₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A train travels at a speed of 66 km/h and halts at five junctions for a certain time. It covers a distance of 1485 km in one day. For how long (in minutes) does the train stop at each junction, if it halts for the same period of time at all the junctions?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the train = 66 km/h

**Concept used:**

Distance = Speed × time

**Calculation:**

Without stoppage train moves 66 × 24 = 1584 kms

For stoppage it is moving 1584 – 1485 = 99 km less

Time takes to cover 99 km by the train = 99/66 = 1.5 hours or 90 min

So, duration of each stops = 90/5 = 18 min

**∴**** Required answer is 18 minutes **

questions.question: A policeman received information that a thief is at a distance of 1.5 km from him. The thief starts moving by car and the policeman chases him by car. The thief and the policeman are moving at the speeds of 90 km/h and 120 km/h respectively. At what distance (in km) will the police catch the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between policeman and thief = 1.5 km

Speed of the thief = 90 km/h

Speed of the policeman = 120 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Speed of policeman - Speed of thief

Distance = Relative speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Relative speed = 120 km/h - 90 km/h

Relative speed = 30 km/h

Let the time taken to catch the thief be t hours.

Distance covered by the policeman in time t = Distance covered by the thief in time t + Initial distance

120t = 90t + 1.5

⇒ 120t - 90t = 1.5

⇒ 30t = 1.5

⇒ t = 1.5 / 30

⇒ t = 0.05 hours

Distance at which the policeman catches the thief = Speed of policeman × Time

Distance = 120 km/h × 0.05 hours

Distance = 6 km

**The police will catch the thief at a distance of 6 km.**

questions.question: Arun and Bhaskar run a race of 3 km. First, Arun gives Bhaskar a head start of 400 m and beats him by 30 seconds. While coming back, Arun gives Bhaskar a lead of 2.5 minutes and gets beaten by 500 m. What is the difference between the times in minutes in which Arun and Bhaskar can run the race for one side separately?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let TA and TB be the times in minutes to run 3000 m.

Case 1: Arun runs 3000 m while Bhaskar runs 2600 m and loses by 0.5 min.

⇒ TA = (2600 ÷ 3000) × TB − 0.5 ⇒ TA = (13/15)TB − 0.5

Case 2: Bhaskar runs 3000 m while Arun runs 2500 m starting 2.5 min late.

⇒ TB = (2500 ÷ 3000) × TA + 2.5 ⇒ TB = (5/6)TA + 2.5

Substitute TB: TA = (13/15)((5/6)TA + 2.5) − 0.5 ⇒ (5/18)TA = 5/3 ⇒ TA = 6 min, TB = 7.5 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 3 km = 3000 m.

Case 1: Bhaskar head start = 400 m, Arun beats him by 30 s = 0.5 min.

Case 2: Bhaskar time lead = 2.5 min, Arun beaten by 500 m.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 0 m 3000 m 
 Case 1: Arun (3000m) wins by 0.5 min 
 Bhaskar (2600m) starting at 400m 
 Case 2: Bhaskar (3000m) wins 
 Arun (2500m) starting 2.5 min late 
 

Let VA and VB be the speeds of Arun and Bhaskar in m/min.

⇒ Case 1: 3000 ÷ VA = (3000 − 400) ÷ VB − 0.5

⇒ 3000 ÷ VA = 2600 ÷ VB − 0.5 --- (1)

⇒ Case 2: (3000 − 500) ÷ VA = 3000 ÷ VB − 2.5

⇒ 2500 ÷ VA = 3000 ÷ VB − 2.5 --- (2)

⇒ From (1), 1/VA = (2600/VB − 0.5) ÷ 3000

⇒ Substitute in (2): 2500 × [(2600/VB − 0.5) ÷ 3000] = 3000/VB − 2.5

⇒ (5/6) × (2600/VB − 0.5) = 3000/VB − 2.5

⇒ 13000/(6VB) − 2.5/6 = 3000/VB − 2.5

⇒ 2.5 − 5/12 = 3000/VB − 6500/(3VB)

⇒ 25/12 = (9000 − 6500) ÷ (3VB) ⇒ 25/12 = 2500 ÷ (3VB)

⇒ 3VB = (2500 × 12) ÷ 25 ⇒ 3VB = 1200 ⇒ VB = 400 m/min

⇒ Time for Bhaskar (TB) = 3000 ÷ 400 = 7.5 min

⇒ Substitute VB in (1): 3000 ÷ VA = 2600 ÷ 400 − 0.5 = 6.5 − 0.5 = 6 min

⇒ Time for Arun (TA) = 6 min

⇒ Difference = 7.5 − 6 = 1.5 min

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Head Start vs Time Lead

A head start of 'x' meters means the opponent starts 'x' meters ahead. A time lead of 't' minutes means the opponent starts 't' minutes earlier than the other person.

Beating by Distance vs Time

If A beats B by 'd' meters, B is 'd' meters behind when A finishes. If A beats B by 't' minutes, B takes 't' minutes more than A to cover the same distance.

Relative Speed in Races

In a linear race, if both run in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = |VA − VB|.

questions.question: For the first part of her journey, Sunita traveled at a speed of 450 m/min and, for the rest of the journey, at a speed 1.4 times her initial speed. If Sunita traveled a total distance of 33.3 km in 1 hour, what was the distance that Sunita traveled at a lower speed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed₁ = 450 meter/min

speed₂ = 1.4 × (speed₁)

The total distance traveled in one hour = 33.3 km

**Concept Used:**

Average speed = total distance/total time

**Calculation:**

Speed₁ = 450 m/min = 450 × 3/50 km/h = 27 km/ h

Speed₂ = 1.4 × (speed₁) = 1.4 × 27 = 37.8 km/h

Total distance traveled in 1 hour = 33.3 km

Let the distance travelled at two speeds be x and (33.3 – x) km

⇒ T₁ + T₂ = 1 hour

⇒ x/S₁ + (33.3 – x)/S₂ = 1

⇒ x/27 + (33.3 – x)/27×1.4 = 1

⇒ (33.3 – x)/ 27 × 1.4 = 1 – x/27

⇒ (33.3 – x)/1.4 = 27 – x

⇒ 33.3 – x = 27 × 1.4 – 1.4x

⇒ 0.4x = 27 × 1.4 – 33.3

⇒ x = (37.8 – 33.3)/0.4

⇒ x = 4.5/0.4 = 11.25 km

**∴ The distance traveled by Sunita at a lower speed is 11.25 km.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Calculation:
